bottleneck.description: Largest US sidewalk delivery robot fleet (~2,000 units) with anchor Uber Eats partnership, operating in a contested last-mile autonomous delivery market with multiple peer alternatives.

dependency.key_customers: Uber Eats (anchor platform partner), DoorDash, Shake Shack, White Castle, regional restaurant brands across LA, Miami, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, Atlanta
dependency.key_suppliers: Nvidia (compute), Magna International (manufacturing partner for Gen 3 robots), various sensor/lidar/camera suppliers (not single-sourced)

editorial.notes: Sidewalk delivery is a competitive market with multiple credible operators (Starship Technologies with the largest global fleet, Coco Robotics, Kiwibot, Cartken/Mitsubishi, Avride/Yandex) and substitutes from drone delivery (Zipline, Wing) and human-courier gig platforms. Serve has scale-leader position in the US sidewalk niche but no proprietary bottleneck input, and the Uber Eats relationship is commercial rather than exclusive. LOW is consistent with the SYM warehouse-automation calibration anchor — contested operational-automation market with no structural choke-point.
